gaps.sentence: I will note the reference number in case I ___ it later.
gaps.hint: in case means as a precaution
gaps.explanation: 'In case' describes a precaution and takes the present simple: need.

gaps.sentence: If this medicine ___ relief within an hour, call me back.
gaps.explanation: Conditional instructions use the present simple in the if-clause: does not bring.

gaps.sentence: You will not pass the course unless you ___ all the assignments.
gaps.hint: unless means if not, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' introduces a negative condition and takes the present simple: complete.

gaps.sentence: If the hotel ___ a pool, we would book it for the whole team.
gaps.hint: unreal present lack of a facility
gaps.explanation: The hotel does not have a pool now, so the if-clause takes the past simple: had.

gaps.sentence: If you mix blue and yellow, you always ___ green.
gaps.explanation: The adverb 'always' signals a timeless result, so the present simple fits: get.

gaps.sentence: As long as you ___ the rules, you will have no problems here.
gaps.hint: as long as states the condition
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' introduces the condition and takes the present simple: follow.

gaps.sentence: If only I ___ faster — we might still catch the train.
gaps.hint: if only plus could, present inability
gaps.explanation: 'If only' plus 'could' expresses a present inability you regret: could run.

gaps.sentence: If the pain ___, stop taking the tablets and call your doctor.
gaps.hint: medical instruction with present after if
gaps.explanation: Conditional instructions use the present simple in the if-clause: gets worse.
